title: Set 94

sentences.ko: 삼촌이 저녁 먹는 내내 우리 언제 집 살 거냐고 물어봤어요. 사촌이 봄에 집을 하나 샀다고 그 얘기를 놓질 않는 거예요. 지금 집값이 미쳤다고 했더니, 자기네 살 때도 미친 값이었다고 하더라고요. 그런 말에 뭐라고 해야 돼요? 틀린 말은 아닌데, 삼촌은 1994년에 산 거잖아요.
sentences.text: My uncle spent the whole dinner asking when we're buying a house, and he would not let it go, because his daughter just bought one in the spring. So I said prices are insane right now, and he goes, well, they were insane when we bought too. What do you even say to that? He's not wrong, but he bought his in 1994.

alts.text: So my uncle would not drop it at dinner, kept asking when we're gonna buy a house, cause his daughter just got one in the spring. I told him prices are nuts right now, and he's like, yeah, they were nuts when we bought too. What are you even supposed to say to that? He's not wrong, but he bought his in 1994.

My uncle spent the entire dinner asking when we intend to buy a house, and he would not drop the subject, because his daughter purchased one in the spring. I said that prices are extremely high at the moment, and he replied that they were just as high when they bought theirs. What is one meant to say to that? He is not wrong, but he bought his in 1994.

sentences.note: **let it go** 는 하던 얘기를 그만 접는다는 뜻이에요. 여기서는 안 접고 계속 물고 늘어진다는 말이죠. **he goes** 는 he said 대신 쓰는 구어체로, 남의 말을 옮길 때 자주 씁니다. **insane** 은 값이 말도 안 되게 비싸다고 할 때 쓰는 과장 표현이에요.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 어제 회사 앞에서 샌드위치랑 커피를 샀는데 19달러가 나왔어요. 잘못 봤나 싶어서 한참 서 있었어요. 2년째 다니던 데인데! 그래서 지금은 도시락 싸 다니는 사람이 됐어요. 나는 절대 안 그럴 거라고 했었는데. 사 먹는 데 한 달에 200달러가 나가고 있었으니, 이제 그걸 알고도 모르는 척은 못 하겠더라고요.
sentences.text: I got a sandwich and a coffee by my office yesterday and it came to nineteen dollars, and I stood there thinking I'd read it wrong. It's the same place I've been going to for two years! So now I'm the guy bringing lunch in a bag, which I said I'd never do, but eating out was costing me two hundred a month and I can't pretend I don't know that now.

alts.text: Grabbed a sandwich and a coffee by my office yesterday and it rang up at nineteen dollars, and I just stood there figuring I'd misread it. Same place I've been going to for two years! So now I'm the guy with lunch in a bag, which I swore I'd never do, but eating out was running me two hundred a month and I can't pretend I don't know that now.

I purchased a sandwich and a coffee near my office yesterday, and the total came to nineteen dollars, and I stood there thinking I had misread it. It is the same place I have been going to for two years. So I am now the person who brings lunch in a bag, which I said I would never do, but eating out was costing me two hundred a month, and I cannot pretend I am unaware of that now.

sentences.note: **it came to nineteen dollars** 의 come to 는 합계가 얼마 나왔다는 뜻이에요. **I'm the guy bringing lunch in a bag** 처럼 I'm the guy 로 시작하면 내가 그런 부류의 사람이 됐다는 자조 섞인 표현이 됩니다. **I can't pretend I don't know that** 은 알고도 모른 척할 수는 없다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 제가 시간을 뺄 수 있는 주는 11월 첫째 주뿐이에요. 그 다음 주말에는 결혼식에 서야 하고, 그 뒤로는 12월까지 일정이 꽉 차 있거든요. 그쪽 일정을 일주일 앞당길 수 있어요? 아니면 그때가 부모님 오시는 때인가요? 더 미룰 거면 솔직히 그냥 봄까지 기다리는 게 나을 것 같아요.
sentences.text: The only week I can actually get away is that first week of November, because I'm in a wedding the weekend after that and then I'm booked solid until December. Can you move yours up a week, or is that when your parents are in town? Because if we push it any later I'd honestly rather just wait until spring.

alts.text: First week of November is the only week I can actually get out, cause I'm in a wedding the weekend after that and then I'm slammed till December. Can you bump yours up a week, or is that when your parents are in town? Cause if we push it any later I'd honestly rather just wait for spring.

The only week I am genuinely able to get away is the first week of November, because I am in a wedding the following weekend and am then fully booked until December. Would you be able to move yours forward by a week, or is that when your parents will be in town? If we postpone it any further, I would honestly prefer to wait until spring.

sentences.note: **get away** 는 일에서 빠져나와 어디 다녀온다는 뜻이에요. 휴가 얘기에 자주 나옵니다. **booked solid** 는 일정이 빈틈없이 꽉 찼다는 말이고, **move yours up a week** 의 move up 은 일정을 일주일 앞당긴다는 뜻이에요. 뒤로 미루는 건 push it later 라고 합니다.

sentences.ko: 7월에 그 큰 에스프레소 머신 샀잖아요, 제가 계속 보여 주던 거요. 그런데 네 번쯤 썼어요. 기계가 나빠서가 아니에요. 내리는 데 15분이 걸리는데 저는 7시에 집을 나서야 하니까 그냥 가는 길에 하나 사 마셔요. 게다가 아내는 그게 조리대 반을 차지하고 있는데 한마디도 안 해요. 차라리 뭐라고 한마디 했으면 나았을 것 같아요.
sentences.text: I bought that big espresso machine in July, the one I kept showing you, and I've used it maybe four times. It's not that it's bad. It's that it takes fifteen minutes and I'm out the door at seven, so I just grab something on the way. And my wife hasn't said one word about it sitting there taking up half the counter, which is somehow worse than if she had just said something.

alts.text: That big espresso machine I kept showing you? Got it in July and I've used it maybe four times. It's not that it's bad. It takes fifteen minutes and I'm out the door at seven, so I just grab something on the way. And my wife hasn't said a word about it sitting there hogging half the counter, which is somehow worse than if she'd just said something.

I purchased that large espresso machine in July, the one I kept showing you, and I have used it perhaps four times. It is not that it is bad. It is that it takes fifteen minutes, and I leave the house at seven, so I simply pick up something on the way. And my wife has not said a single word about it sitting there occupying half the counter, which is somehow worse than if she had said something.

sentences.note: **It's not that it's bad** 는 그게 나빠서가 아니라고 오해를 먼저 막아 두는 말이에요. 뒤에 진짜 이유가 따라옵니다. **taking up half the counter** 의 take up 은 자리를 차지한다는 뜻이고, **I'm out the door at seven** 은 7시에 집을 나선다는 관용 표현이에요.

sentences.ko: 토요일을 통째로 조카 축구 경기장 접이식 의자에 앉아서 보냈어요. 조카 엄마가 일을 해야 해서 누구라도 가 있어야 했거든요. 경기가 여섯 개였는데 조카는 그중 두 경기만 뛰었어요. 그리고 일요일에는 아무것도 안 했어요. 목 뒤가 햇볕에 타서 의자에 등을 기댈 수도 없었거든요. 그쪽 주말은 어땠어요?
sentences.text: I spent all of Saturday in a folding chair at my nephew's soccer thing, because my sister had to work and somebody had to be there. Six games, and he was in two of them. Then Sunday I didn't do anything at all, because I got sunburned on the back of my neck and I couldn't even lean back in a chair. How was yours?

alts.text: Spent my whole Saturday in a folding chair at my nephew's soccer thing, cause my sister had to work and somebody had to show up. Six games, and he was in two of them. Then Sunday I did nothing at all, cause I got sunburned on the back of my neck and I couldn't even lean back in a chair. How was yours?

I spent the entirety of Saturday in a folding chair at my nephew's soccer event, because my sister had to work and someone needed to be there. There were six games, and he was in two of them. Then on Sunday I did nothing at all, because I had gotten sunburned on the back of my neck and could not even lean back in a chair. How was yours?

sentences.note: **my nephew's soccer thing** 의 thing 은 정확한 이름을 모르거나 굳이 밝힐 필요가 없을 때 뭉뚱그려 쓰는 말이에요. **I got sunburned** 는 햇볕에 살이 탔다는 뜻이고, **lean back** 은 등을 뒤로 기댄다는 말입니다.

reviewed: 4번 한국어 끝에 영어에 없는 "더 무서워요"가 붙어 있었습니다. 영어는 "차라리 한마디 했으면 나았겠다"까지만 말하므로 한국어도 거기서 끊었습니다.
4번 한국어 "네 번쯤 썼나 봐요"는 자기가 한 일을 추측하는 말투라 어색해서 "네 번쯤 썼어요"로 고쳤습니다.
4번 casual 의 "eating half the counter"는 원어민이 쓰지 않는 꼴입니다(쓰려면 eating up). 더 구어다운 "hogging half the counter"로 바꿨습니다.
1번 formal 의 "they were just as high when they bought as well"은 just as high 와 as well 이 겹쳐 어색해서 "when they bought theirs"로 정리했습니다.
